chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from his father, from Abu al-Maghra' Humayd ibn al-Muthanna, from Sama'ah, from al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him), that he asked him about the slaughtered meat of the Jew and the Christian, so he said:

key_terms.لَا تَقْرَبُوهَا: Do not approach it (i.e., do not eat or use it)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat of Jews and Christians in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfahar, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a general prohibition against consuming the meat of Jews and Christians, reflecting the view that their specific ritual slaughter lacks the requisite Islamic invocation of God's name. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between the permissibility of 'People of the Book' in general and the specific validity of their slaughter practices, often cited alongside the verse on 'food of those who were given the Scripture.'
